subject: P4 Math
sourceNote: Lesson structure rebuilt from the uploaded book index and exercises.

modules.title: Big Numbers! & Changing Values
modules.summary: Read large whole numbers and explain how a digit's value changes with its place.
terms: Read large whole numbers and explain how a digit's value changes with its place.

questions.text: What is the value of the digit 8 in 583,460,905?
Complete: 1,000,000 is one ______.
State the digit in the ten-millions place of 3,418,079,265.
Explain why the same digit can have different values in different places.
questions.answer: A digit's value depends on its place in the number.

modules.title: Many Forms to Write Numbers
modules.summary: Write whole numbers in standard, word and expanded forms.
terms: Write whole numbers in standard, word and expanded forms.

questions.text: Write 45,006 in expanded form.
Which is the word form of 102,004?
Why is zero sometimes needed inside a standard-form number?
questions.answer: It holds an empty place value.

modules.title: Composing and Decomposing Numbers
modules.summary: Compose and decompose multi-digit numbers in more than one way.
terms: Compose and decompose multi-digit numbers in more than one way.

questions.text: Decompose 326,405 by place value.
Which composition equals 70,305?
Give a second valid decomposition of 4,000 using thousands and hundreds.

modules.title: Comparing Big Numbers
modules.summary: Compare multi-digit whole numbers using place value.
terms: Compare multi-digit whole numbers using place value.

questions.text: Which is greater: 650,201 or 605,210?
Explain the first place you compare when two numbers have the same number of digits.
questions.answer: Start from the greatest place value on the left.

modules.title: Descending and Ascending Numbers
modules.summary: Order whole numbers from least to greatest or greatest to least.
terms: Order whole numbers from least to greatest or greatest to least.

questions.text: Arrange 56,210; 506,021; 43,692 from least to greatest.
Which list is descending?
Ascending means from ______ to greatest.
Why is place value useful when ordering large numbers?
questions.answer: It lets us compare digits from the greatest place first.

modules.title: Rounding Rules
modules.summary: Round whole numbers to a given place value.
terms: Round whole numbers to a given place value.

questions.text: Round 47,638 to the nearest thousand.
Round 6,449 to the nearest hundred.
When rounding to the nearest ten, a ones digit of 5 rounds up.
Explain which digit you inspect when rounding to the nearest thousand.

modules.title: Properties of Addition
modules.summary: Use commutative, associative and identity properties of addition.
terms: Use commutative, associative and identity properties of addition.

questions.text: (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4) shows the associative property.
Why can regrouping addends help mental calculation?
questions.answer: It can create easier sums without changing the total.

modules.title: Addition with Regrouping
modules.summary: Add multi-digit whole numbers accurately using regrouping.
terms: Add multi-digit whole numbers accurately using regrouping.

questions.text: A library has 18,450 books and receives 3,275 more. How many books now?

modules.title: Subtraction with Regrouping
modules.summary: Subtract multi-digit whole numbers accurately using regrouping.
terms: Subtract multi-digit whole numbers accurately using regrouping.

questions.text: A store had 25,000 items and sold 7,860. How many remain?

modules.title: Bar Models, Variables and Story Problems
modules.summary: Represent unknowns and relationships in story problems with bar models and variables.
terms: Represent unknowns and relationships in story problems with bar models and variables.

questions.text: Mona has 35 stickers. She gets x more and now has 52. Find x.
A letter such as x can represent an ______ quantity.
Explain how a bar model helps in a story problem.
questions.answer: It shows known and unknown parts and their relationship.

modules.title: Multistep Story Problems
modules.summary: Solve multistep problems using addition and subtraction and check reasonableness.
terms: Solve multistep problems using addition and subtraction and check reasonableness.

questions.text: A shop sold 1,250 items Monday and 980 Tuesday, then 300 were returned. Net sold?
Which should be done first in 4,000 + 700 - 250?
Why should you check whether a multistep answer is reasonable?
questions.answer: To detect operation or calculation errors.

modules.title: Measuring Length
modules.summary: Choose and convert suitable metric length units.
terms: Choose and convert suitable metric length units.

questions.text: Which unit is most suitable for the length of a pencil?
1 meter = ______ centimeters.
A ribbon is 2 m long. How many centimeters?

modules.title: Measuring Mass
modules.summary: Choose and use suitable metric mass units.
terms: Choose and use suitable metric mass units.

questions.text: Which unit is suitable for the mass of a school bag?
1 kilogram = ______ grams.
A box has a mass of 4 kg. What is it in grams?

modules.title: Units of Capacity
modules.summary: Choose and use suitable metric capacity units.
terms: Choose and use suitable metric capacity units.

questions.text: Which unit is suitable for a bottle of water?
1 liter = ______ milliliters.
Two 500 mL bottles contain how many liters altogether?

modules.title: Units of Time & Elapsed Time
modules.summary: Relate time units and calculate elapsed time.
terms: Relate time units and calculate elapsed time.

questions.text: 1 day = ______ hours.
1 week = ______ days.
A bike ride starts at 8:15 A.M. and lasts 3 h 26 min. When does it finish?

modules.title: Applications of Measurement 1
modules.summary: Apply measurement relationships in real situations.
terms: Apply measurement relationships in real situations.

questions.text: A rope is 3 m 40 cm and another is 2 m 75 cm. Total length?
A tank has 5 L. 1,250 mL is used. How much remains?
Why must units be converted before adding some measurements?
questions.answer: Quantities must be expressed in compatible units.

modules.title: Applications of Measurement 2
modules.summary: Solve multistep measurement problems and explain units.
terms: Solve multistep measurement problems and explain units.

questions.text: A rope is 3 m 40 cm and another is 2 m 75 cm. Total length?
A tank has 5 L. 1,250 mL is used. How much remains?
Why must units be converted before adding some measurements?
questions.answer: Quantities must be expressed in compatible units.

modules.title: Finding Perimeter
modules.summary: Find perimeter by adding side lengths or using formulas.
terms: Find perimeter by adding side lengths or using formulas.

questions.text: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 12 cm by 17 cm.
Find the perimeter of a square with side 8 km.
Which formula finds rectangle perimeter?
Why is perimeter measured in linear units?
questions.answer: It measures distance around the boundary.

modules.title: Finding Area
modules.summary: Find area of rectangles and squares using multiplication.
terms: Find area of rectangles and squares using multiplication.

questions.text: Find the area of a rectangle 10 cm by 7 cm.
Find the area of a square with side 6 cm.
Which formula finds rectangle area?
Why is area measured in square units?
questions.answer: It counts how many unit squares cover a surface.

modules.title: Unknown Dimensions
modules.summary: Use area or perimeter information to find an unknown side length.
terms: Use area or perimeter information to find an unknown side length.

questions.text: A rectangle has area 48 cm² and width 6 cm. Find length.
A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 9 cm. Find width.
If area = length × width, then length = area ÷ ______.
Area 63 cm²; width 7 cm; length = ______.

modules.title: Complex Shapes
modules.summary: Find area or perimeter of composite shapes by splitting them into simpler shapes.
terms: Find area or perimeter of composite shapes by splitting them into simpler shapes.

questions.text: A composite shape is split into rectangles of areas 24 cm² and 18 cm². Total area?
A complex shape can often be split into simpler rectangles.
Why should shared internal edges not be counted in the outside perimeter?
questions.answer: They are not part of the outside boundary.

questions.text: Two non-overlapping rectangles have areas 20 and 35. Combined area?

modules.title: Multiplicative Comparison
modules.summary: Interpret statements such as 'times as many' and write multiplication comparisons.
terms: Interpret statements such as 'times as many' and write multiplication comparisons.

questions.text: '24 is 4 times as many as 6' is represented by:
Sara has 5 stickers. Omar has 3 times as many. How many?
7 × 8 = 56 means 56 is ______ times 8.
Explain the difference between '3 more than' and '3 times as many'.
questions.answer: The first uses addition; the second uses multiplication.

modules.title: Creating and Solving Multiplicative Comparison Equations
modules.summary: Write and solve equations that represent multiplicative comparisons.
terms: Write and solve equations that represent multiplicative comparisons.

questions.text: A tree is 4 times as tall as a 2 m plant. Write and solve an equation.
Which equation shows 35 is 5 times 7?
Why is a variable useful in a comparison equation?

modules.title: Commutative, Identity and Zero Properties
modules.summary: Apply basic multiplication properties to simplify calculations.
terms: Apply basic multiplication properties to simplify calculations.

questions.text: 4 × 6 = 6 × 4 shows the commutative property.

modules.title: Associative Property & Multiplication Patterns
modules.summary: Use grouping and patterns to reason about products.
terms: Use grouping and patterns to reason about products.

questions.text: The associative property changes the ______, not the order, of factors.
How can patterns make multiplication faster?
questions.answer: Known products can be extended using place value or grouping.

modules.title: Identifying Factors of Whole Numbers
modules.summary: List factor pairs of whole numbers.
terms: List factor pairs of whole numbers.

questions.text: List all factors of 12.
Which is a factor of 18?
1 is a factor of every whole number.
How do factor pairs help find all factors?
questions.answer: Each pair multiplies to the number and lists two factors.

modules.title: Prime and Composite Numbers
modules.summary: Classify whole numbers as prime or composite using their factors.
terms: Classify whole numbers as prime or composite using their factors.

questions.text: Which number is prime?
Which number is composite?
A prime number has exactly ______ positive factors.
Why is 1 neither prime nor composite?
questions.answer: It has only one positive factor.

modules.title: Greatest Common Factor (G.C.F.)
modules.summary: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers.
terms: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers.

questions.text: The G.C.F. is the ______ common factor.
Why can G.C.F. help make equal groups with no leftovers?
questions.answer: It is the largest size that divides both quantities exactly.

modules.title: Multiples and Common Multiples
modules.summary: Generate multiples and identify common multiples.
terms: Generate multiples and identify common multiples.

questions.text: Write the first five positive multiples of 6.
Which is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
24 is a multiple of 8.
How are multiples generated?
questions.answer: Multiply the number by whole numbers.

modules.title: Relationships Between Factors and Multiples
modules.summary: Explain the inverse relationship between factors and multiples.
terms: Explain the inverse relationship between factors and multiples.

questions.text: If 5 is a factor of 30, then 30 is a ______ of 5.
If a divides b exactly, then b is a multiple of a.
Which pair shows a correct factor-multiple relationship?
Explain how factors and multiples are related.
questions.answer: A factor divides a number exactly; that number is a multiple of the factor.

modules.title: Area Model Strategy & Distributive Property
modules.summary: Use an area model and distributive property to multiply.
terms: Use an area model and distributive property to multiply.

questions.text: Use distributive thinking: 23 × 4 = (20 × 4) + (3 × 4) = ______.
An area model can split a factor into tens and ones.
Why does the distributive property work in an area model?
questions.answer: The total area equals the sum of the smaller partial areas.

modules.title: Partial Products & Multiply by a One-Digit Number
modules.summary: Multiply multi-digit numbers using partial products.
terms: Multiply multi-digit numbers using partial products.

questions.text: Partial products come from multiplying each place-value ______.
Explain one advantage of partial products.
questions.answer: It shows the contribution of each place value clearly.

modules.title: Multiply a Two-Digit Number by a Multiple of 10
modules.summary: Use place-value patterns to multiply by multiples of ten.
terms: Use place-value patterns to multiply by multiples of ten.

questions.text: Why can 30 be treated as 3 × 10 when multiplying?
questions.answer: It uses place value and multiplication properties.

modules.title: Exploring Remainders
modules.summary: Interpret remainders in division situations.

questions.text: 29 students ride in cars holding 4 each. How many cars are needed?
In 17 ÷ 5, the remainder is:
Why can the same remainder be interpreted differently in different problems?
questions.answer: The context may require rounding up, ignoring, or reporting the remainder.

modules.title: Patterns in Division
modules.summary: Use place-value and fact patterns to reason about quotients.
terms: Use place-value and fact patterns to reason about quotients.

questions.text: How does place value help with division patterns?
questions.answer: Scaling a dividend by powers of ten scales the quotient predictably when the divisor stays fixed.

modules.title: Area Model and Division
modules.summary: Use area models to represent division.
terms: Use area models to represent division.

questions.text: Split 84 into 80 + 4 to divide by 4. What is the quotient?
An area model can show division as finding an unknown side length.
Why is decomposing the dividend useful?
questions.answer: It creates easier partial divisions that can be added.

modules.title: Partial Quotients & Standard Division Algorithm
modules.summary: Divide multi-digit numbers using partial quotients and the standard algorithm.
terms: Divide multi-digit numbers using partial quotients and the standard algorithm.

questions.text: Partial quotients subtract convenient ______ of the divisor.
How can multiplication check 936 ÷ 8 = 117?

modules.title: Division and Multiplication
modules.summary: Use multiplication to check division and relate fact families.
terms: Use multiplication to check division and relate fact families.

questions.text: Which multiplication checks 84 ÷ 7 = 12?
Multiplication and division are inverse operations.
Why is multiplication a useful way to check division?
questions.answer: Multiplying quotient by divisor should reproduce the dividend when there is no remainder.

modules.title: Order of Operations & Story Problems
modules.summary: Evaluate numerical expressions in the correct order and apply them to story problems.
terms: Evaluate numerical expressions in the correct order and apply them to story problems.

questions.text: What is the first operation in 18 - 15 + 3 × 8 - 2?
Why are parentheses important in numerical expressions?
questions.answer: They show which calculation must be done first.
